topics.topic: Outcome classification when a trap and unconfirmed cleanup occur together
questions: If an execution records a trap, does not time out or exhaust resources, and its cleanup cannot be confirmed, is its outcome `sandbox_violation` or `crashed` with `cleanup_failed`?

quotes: A03-3: trap_raised AND NOT (timeout OR resource_exhausted) -> outcome = sandbox_violation   (even if output conforms)

11. A03-5: When removal of the exchange directory cannot be confirmed, the execution is
    recorded `crashed` with detail `cleanup_failed`, its output is discarded and
    the kernel process stops.
judgement.why: The first passage classifies every trapped execution without timeout or resource exhaustion as `sandbox_violation`, while the second classifies the same execution as `crashed` with `cleanup_failed` when cleanup is also unconfirmed.

bases.passage: A03-3: trap_raised AND NOT (timeout OR resource_exhausted) -> outcome = sandbox_violation   (even if output conforms)
bases.rests_on:
Outcomes are closed and checked in this order, the first that holds
   deciding: wall deadline passed — `timeout`; a limit hit (memory, process count,
   scratch, `output_bytes`) — `resource_exhausted`; a trap of rule 4 raised —
   `sandbox_violation`; the module failed to load, has no `run`, raised, or the
   process exited abnormally — `crashed`; the returned dict does not have exactly
   the output ports, or a value fails its port's schema, or a file output is not
   `bytes` — `contract_violation`; otherwise the execution succeeded.

bases.passage:
11. A03-5: When removal of the exchange directory cannot be confirmed, the execution is
    recorded `crashed` with detail `cleanup_failed`, its output is discarded and
    the kernel process stops.
bases.rests_on:
An execution completes only after every process of the environment is reaped
   and the exchange directory is removed. If that cannot be confirmed the output
   is discarded, the execution is recorded `crashed` with detail
   `cleanup_failed`, and the kernel process stops; runs it left `running` are
   recovered on the next start (A14 rule 5).

witness.initial: An active flow contains a function whose implementation catches the exception from `time.time()` and returns a conforming output, under bounds that are not exhausted.
events: An owner or agent starts the run.
The function calls `time.time()`; the runner records the trap, and the function catches the exception and returns a conforming output.
`module:sandbox` cannot confirm removal of the exchange directory.
After restart, an owner or agent reads the function element's NodeExecution from the trace.
outcomes: The NodeExecution status is `sandbox_violation` because the trap was raised and neither timeout nor resource exhaustion occurred.
The NodeExecution status is `crashed` with detail `cleanup_failed` because cleanup could not be confirmed.
witness.observer: The owner or agent reading the run trace.
basis:
`module:surface` checks the request's token against
`capability:installation.current_token_list` (A16 rules 1–2) and admits the request; the owner or any agent may run (A16 rule
3), and it answers only once the run rests or ends (A18 rule 3).

Each trap, before raising, writes its hit to the
   runner's channel to the parent, which user code cannot unsend; any recorded hit makes the
   execution `sandbox_violation` under the order of rule 5, even when the code
   catches it and returns a conforming output: `timeout` and `resource_exhausted`
   still come first.

An execution completes only after every process of the environment is reaped
   and the exchange directory is removed. If that cannot be confirmed the output
   is discarded, the execution is recorded `crashed` with detail
   `cleanup_failed`, and the kernel process stops; runs it left `running` are
   recovered on the next start (A14 rule 5).

The trace record of one concluded attempt at one node, or of a node that was not
executed because its guards disabled it or an upstream node failed (K-09). Read by the owner
and agents reading traces, by repair (K-12) and by capture into a trial corpus.
